# autonomy

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
*The envelope and orchestrator of verifiably: what may run unattended*

What may run unattended, under what tier, and how the next research action is chosen: the run baseline and dispositions, tiers as write-class permits, the actor sandbox and session ledger, behavioural profiles and the versioned priority function. It drives science's commands as tools and holds no private kernel access. The envelope's first half is built: tiers, the closing check, and the sandbox.
<!-- ops:identity end -->

## Documentation

- [User and autonomy layer design](https://github.com/verifiably/beliefs/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-user-and-autonomy-layer-design.md)
  — the governing design, in the kernel repository: §7 is this layer, §8 orders the
  sub-projects. Work here starts at sub-project #6, the envelope, after the command
  framework, and ends with #7, the loop and the priority function (`science.priority.v1`).
- This repository's own designs and plans are under [docs/specs](docs/specs) and
  [docs/plans](docs/plans); the envelope's design is
  `docs/specs/2026-10-12-envelope-design.md`.
- This layer is split from `science` on code-lineage independence: the envelope must
  not share a package with the surface it constrains, so its only seam is `science`'s
  commands as tools.
